1.d4 d5 2.c4 c5 3.cxd5 Nf6.name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Austrian Defence, Gusev Countergambit

1.d4 d5 2.c4 c5 3.cxd5 Nf6 4.e4.strategy: The critical reply: the pawn defends d5 and takes space, and White offers the e-pawn rather than defend passively. If Black takes it, White wins the c5 pawn and stays a pawn up with an open centre, so Black has to generate play by force.

1.d4 d5 2.c4 c5 3.cxd5 Nf6 4.e4 Nxe4.strategy: Takes the offered pawn at once and centralises the knight. The cost is time: the knight has moved twice, White can take c5 next, and Black must use the lead in development to create threats.
